messages: maria: heads-up: mkdocs linkcheck spiked on the docs migration — several relative snippet links from /guides/sdk-usage to /examples break after TOC reflow. maria: CI snippet: ``` Linkcheck: ERROR - 'guides/sdk-usage.md' broken reference 'examples/python/streaming.md#start-stream' Found 5 broken links ``` ben: seems the slugify behavior changed (underscores -> dashes). that will break any anchor that used underscores. olivia: is it just anchors or also file path case? we saw a windows-relpath case earlier. maria: primarily anchors here. one example file still has an explicit id with underscore, so mismatch both ways. sam: options: mass-update links to dashes, add explicit HTML anchors for legacy ids, or add a mkdocs redirect/alias for old slugs. tradeoffs: mass-update is simplest but noisy in git history. ben: i'd prefer adding explicit HTML anchor tags in the examples for backward compat, and then a followup pass to canonicalize links. olivia: can we add a check to docs-lint to flag underscore anchors so we don't regress? sam: yes, will add a small grep-based lint rule in CI for now. maria: action items: sam to open a small PR that: 1) updates the problematic links in guides to use dashes; 2) inserts above the target heading as a stopgap; 3) add docs-lint rule and a note in migration checklist. sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/427 — includes tests and changelog blurb. docs-bot: Preview build started for fix/doc-anchor-compat (canary). docs-bot: Preview build failed: linkcheck still found 2 references. ben: which ones? maria: CI output shows two remaining references to old internal links from archived_examples.md. i'll patch them in the PR. sam: patched and force-pushed. re-running build. docs-bot: Preview build succeeded. Linkcheck: 0 broken links. olivia: nice. let's schedule a rolling cleanup where we canonicalize all docs to dashes in a separate commit to keep history tidy. maria: added to migration checklist and will ping platform team before the canonical sweep. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
